title: Admin Web V2 Catalog Repair Actions
problem: Admin Web V2 can list Catalog Governance issues, but operators still lack bounded review-plan-driven repair workflows for unknown, low-confidence, missing Provider Mapping, and duplicate-source cases.
gates: cd apps/admin-web && npm run generate:admin-api && npm run check && npm run test -- adminApi/client.test.ts
cd apps/admin-web && npm run check && npm run test -- App.test.tsx adminApi/client.test.ts adminApi/dataSource.test.ts
cd apps/admin-web && npm run check && npm run test && npm run build

evidence.summary: Opened the Catalog Repair Actions lane from AWA closeout and MBG follow-on order; initial inventory found a read-only Catalog Governance list route but no accepted repair detail, review-plan, or mutation routes.

Accepted one Media Item plus one Provider Mapping accept/reject as the first catalog repair action; documented missing detail, review-plan, mutation, generated contract, and redaction requirements before Admin Web UI work.

Implemented redaction-safe Catalog Governance item detail and Provider Mapping review-plan Admin API routes, generated Admin Web contract coverage, client wrappers, HTTP API docs, and focused redaction tests.

Implemented the confirmed Provider Mapping review mutation with idempotent result semantics, generated Admin Web contract coverage, redaction-safe client/data-source wrappers, HTTP API docs, and no-fake-mutation-fallback tests.

Implemented the route-owned Catalog Governance repair UI with queue-to-review navigation, Provider Mapping selection, decision URL state, review-plan preview, explicit confirmation, result/failure states, and unsafe text exclusion tests.

Ran focused Rust/API/Admin Web gates and browser smoke for queue, repair context, review-plan, confirmation success, visible failure, desktop/mobile overflow, console errors, and unsafe text exclusion.
Closed the lane and split broader Catalog Governance repair classes into follow-on work.

continue_policy.notes: Lane complete. Open a new workstream for rematch/provider search, duplicate-source repair, hierarchy repair, NFO writes, arbitrary metadata editing, users/permissions, or Library Access.
